similarity2graph

Create a networkx graph from a provided similarity matrix.

This module loads a pickled similarity matrix file (‘similarity_*.pickle’), filters on edges with a similarity score equal or higher than provided edge threshold, removes duplicated sentences based on provided duplicates threshold, creates a networkx graph from the filtered similarity matrix, and saves the graph as a pickled file.

Usage:

python similarity2graph.py -i similarity_$full_exp_name.pickle -t 0.75 -d 1.0

param -i:

Name of the input file containing the similarity matrix (‘similarity_*.pickle’).

param –input_file:

Name of the input file containing the similarity matrix (‘similarity_*.pickle’).

param -t:

Edge threshold. Only sentences with at least one similarity score equal or higher than this threshold is kept, and edges with lower similarity score than threshold are removed.

param –edge_threshold:

Edge threshold. Only sentences with at least one similarity score equal or higher than this threshold is kept, and edges with lower similarity score than threshold are removed.

param -d:

Duplicates threshold. Only one sentence is kept of duplicated sentences in the corpus.

param –duplicates_threshold:

Duplicates threshold. Only one sentence is kept of duplicated sentences in the corpus.

Input:

A pickled similarity matrix file (‘similarity_*.pickle’). Where for each sentence per row the cosine similarity score is calculated for each sentence in columns.

Output:

A pickled networkx graph file (‘graph_thres_<edge_threshold>_<full_exp_name>.pickle’).

similarity2graph.main()

Create a networkx graph from a provided similarity matrix.

This function is the main entry point of the similarity2graph.py script. It loads a pickled similarity matrix file (‘similarity_*.pickle’), filters on edges with a similarity score equal or higher than provided edge threshold, removes duplicated sentences based on provided duplicates threshold, creates a networkx graph from the filtered similarity matrix, and saves the graph as a pickled file.
